newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded lower on fairly good demand and moderate to heavy offerings for the trading week, USDA said.
Retail demand improved for immediate needs, but at lower price levels. These lower price levels stimulated demand both for immediate and forward interest.
Fairly good interest for the rib cuts was noted for retailers' immediate featuring needs. Consequently, these particular cuts traded higher.
Loin cuts were pressured all week, with most pressure on tenderloins and top butts on both Select and Choice cuts.
Round and chuck cuts also traded lower as these cuts experienced rather light demand early in the week but did show some improved demand later in the week.

Closely trimmed items again traded lower on fairly good demand with the most downward pressure noted on both the chuck and round cuts. Fresh beef trimmings again traded lower on moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse grind items traded lower generally for their immediate needs, but a firmer undertone was noted late in the trading period.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 2.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.50 to 2.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 1.50 to 2.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 2.50 lower; Closely trimmed item's 1.00 to 1.50 lower; Beef trimmings 3.50 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 3.00 to 8.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.40 at 102.76; 700/850 Dn 1.52 at 102.00; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.18 at 96.36; 700/850 Dn 1.00 at 95.65.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The boneless beef market was forced sharply lower as supplies mounted due to lackluster demand. Supplies remained readily available in some areas as product was slow to clear the market channels due to competition with alternative grinding materials. This downfall occurred even though many anticipated slaughter numbers to tighten up as live cow prices continued to be steady.
However, weakness in the live market was noted in some areas. This in return, coupled with light demand pushed the cow carcass market lower.

The cow cuts moved at mostly steady price levels on moderate demand. Utility carcasses 2.00-3.00 lower; Cutter 5,00 lower; 90% boneless beef 8.00-9.00 lower in the Midwest, Texas 6.00-8.00 lower; 85% mostly 7.00 lower; 75% not established; 65% 1.00-3.00 lower.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, June 5, 1997 was estimated at 71.65 per cwt., down 5.05 from a week ago Friday.
